title: Cross-worker media-flow file lock leaks its ticket when beforeEach times out, deadlocking every later test
test: tests/mediaFlowLockHooks.test.js (new): 'a media-flow test that times out in beforeEach waiting for the lock leaves nothing that blocks later tests' and 'the media-flow lock lives under the project outputDir, which Playwright clears when a run starts'. They load the real tests/browser/media-flow.spec.mjs with @playwright/test stubbed (a module.register resolve hook) and drive its hooks the way Playwright does, with two module instances standing for two workers. Also a scratch Playwright harness that runs the real spec file with no web server and a planted holder ticket released when the first test ends (dev-notes/results/check-12-playwright.config.mjs.txt, check-12-setup.mjs.txt, check-12-reporter.mjs.txt, check-12-pw-runs.sh; logs check-12-pw-*.log), run with the Playwright lock held.
proof: The claim holds, on the original code too: tests/browser/media-flow.spec.mjs is byte-identical at ac1c688 and dev 1be0088. beforeEach writes its ticket (lines 525-526) and then waits in for(;;) (529-535). The ticket path reaches loopbackProxyState only after the wait and the proxy listen (587-594), and afterEach returns at once when that is null (602). Playwright 1.63 races each hook against the deadline (worker/workerProcessEntry.js:403-406, Promise.race in TimeoutManager.withRunnable), so on a timeout the hook keeps running and its catch (595-598) never runs. afterEach still runs, because shouldRunAfterEachHooks is set before beforeEach (:1644-1645, :1671-1672). Unit test on the unchanged spec: fails with 'afterEach left the timed-out test queued for the lock' (folder [holder ticket, 1792864080580-0000-...ticket] instead of [holder ticket]) and 'the held lock is not under the project outputDir' (check-12-unit-before.txt). Real Playwright, original spec, 4 s timeout, holder ticket released when test 1 ended: all 12 tests 'Test timeout of 4000ms exceeded while running "beforeEach" hook'. One orphan ticket was added per test and 12 were left, although the holder had released at 4.7 s (check-12-pw-before.log). With outputDir moved elsewhere, a stale ticket in <cwd>/test-results was not cleared by the run start and blocked the test (check-12-pw-outdir-before.log). Fix (cf2a56c): the ticket is tracked from the first line of beforeEach, afterEach marks it abandoned and removes it even when beforeEach never finished, the wait loop and the post-listen step stop on 'abandoned', and the lock folder is path.join(testInfo.project.outputDir, '.media-flow-lock'). After the fix both unit tests pass (check-12-unit-after.txt). Dropping the loop's abandoned check makes the first one fail with 'the abandoned beforeEach is still waiting'. Same Playwright scenario with the server and the 60 s timeout: test 1 times out with only the holder ticket left, tests 2-12 pass, and the folder is empty at the end (check-12-pw-after.log). The outputDir scenario passes, with the stale ticket cleared at the run start. The real playwright.config.mjs gives 12 passed (33.0 s). lint, typecheck and npm test (1014/1014) pass. Overstated in the claim: only the chromium project runs this file. Later tests time out one by one (60 s each) rather than hang. A single Ctrl+C or --max-failures interrupts the test and still runs afterEach, so a holder's ticket was freed and only a waiter's leaked (the same path, now fixed). With fullyParallel false and the lock only in this file, a normal run needs a hard-killed worker or real contention (--fully-parallel, --repeat-each with several workers) for the first unreleased ticket. Left for TASK-092: a hard-killed worker's ticket still blocks the rest of that run, because this fix adds no reclamation. The next run starts clean, because the folder is now in outputDir.
